qt: to the Commission Galato Alexandraki (ECR) Subject:

On 8 July 2026, the Commission decided to refer Greece to the Court of Justice of the European Union because national law still provides for less favourable employment conditions for substitute teachers compared to their permanent colleagues, in particular as regards maternity and sick leave. The referral came after a letter of formal notice was sent in July 2024 and a reasoned opinion in May 2025. In that time, the Greek authorities failed to make the changes required of them and each school year, thousands of teachers continue to work with reduced protections. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Which specific provisions of Greek law are still in breach of Directive 1999/70/EC?
How could it help ensure that substitute teachers are immediately protected until the CJEU delivers its judgment?
Will it call for a specific and binding timetable for the full equalisation of their rights with those of permanent teachers?
